title: Rapid recon CLI and annotated playbook serializer
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a lightweight recon CLI to run ephemeral telemetry probes and a serializer that emits compact, annotated runbook fragments for faster on-call triage. Backwards-compatible; includes docs and integration tests.
description:
Context and motivation:
This PR introduces a small, safe-to-run CLI (rapid-recon) and an annotated playbook serializer designed to speed first-response during incidents. The goal is to make it trivial for an on-call engineer to run a constrained set of probes, collect a compact diagnostic bundle, and generate a condensed runbook snippet that captures the hypothesis, suggested checks, and quick remediation steps.

Why this is different: existing runbook generation required heavy telemetry exports and manual summarization; this adds a low-friction path that (1) runs ephemeral, sandboxed probes, (2) captures minimal telemetry and metadata, (3) serializes the result as an annotated runbook fragment that can be pasted into the incident timeline or Slack. The serializer emits a compact JSON+markdown hybrid for human readability and machine parsing.

High-level changes (summary of commits):
- Add cmd/rapid-recon CLI (go) that coordinates probes with timeouts and safe-mode sandboxing.
- Implement internal/telemetry/sampler service to capture high-precision short-lived spans and a delta sampler to avoid noise.
- Add pkg/playbook/serializer (python) that converts probe outputs into annotated runbook fragments and supports templates with variable interpolation.
- Add webhooks to post a _quick recon card_ to the on-call Slack channel (opt-in feature behind feature flag).
- Unit and integration tests for the sampler and serializer; e2e using the local sandbox harness.

Commits (high-level):
- 1a2b3c4: initial rapid-recon CLI and probe runner loop
- 2b3c4d5: add delta sampler and probe adapters (http, tcp, redis)
- 3c4d5e6: playbook serializer + compact template definitions
- 4d5e6f7: tests, docs, and demo script

Changed files (high level):
- cmd/rapid-recon/main.go
- internal/telemetry/sampler.go
- internal/telemetry/probes/http_probe.go
- pkg/playbook/serializer.py
- pkg/playbook/templates/compact.yaml
- integrations/slack/quick_recon_poster.py
- docs/oncall/rapid-recon.md
- tests/unit/test_serializer.py
- tests/integration/test_recon_e2e.sh

Example of generated runbook fragment (serialized output snippet):
{"summary":"Validate ingress latency and upstream error rates","checks":[{"id":"http-200-check","cmd":"rapid-recon probe http --url https://service.internal/health --timeout 3s","expected":"200","notes":"Runs cached ping against the service; safe-mode disables writes."}],"annotations":"observed spike at 2026-01-29T03:14:12Z, upstream redis RPO high"}

Small code excerpt (serializer output formatting):
playbook_fragment = f"---\nSummary: {summary}\nChecks:\n{checks_markdown}\nAnnotations:\n{annotations}\n---"

Review conversation (high-level):
- Arjun: "Nice concise API for probes. Please ensure probe adapters have strict CPU/memory limits and do not open long-lived connections."
- Maya: "Added timeouts and context cancellation, moved adapters into a worker pool with hard limits. See internal/telemetry/worker_pool.go"
- Evelyn: "Serializer looks solid; can we reduce noise in templates by removing stack traces by default?"
- Maya: "Removed full stack traces, added a `--include-traces` flag for deep debugging."
- Noah: "Minor nit: rename `compact.yaml` -> `condensed.yaml` for clarity."
- Maya: "Applied rename and updated docs."
- Evelyn: "Approved pending CI."
- Arjun: "Approved."

CI summary and iteration: 
- ci/build: pass on first run.
- ci/unit-tests: two failing tests initially (serializer edge-cases) — fixed in 3c4d5e6, rerun -> pass.
- ci/e2e-repro: flaky in sandboxed environment (network bind race); added a retry and explicit ephemeral port selection, rerun -> pass.
- ci/lint: warnings (line-length in generated docs) — fixed in follow-up commit.
- Final status: all checks green and branch protection satisfied.

Safety and rollout notes:
- Feature is behind an opt-in feature flag: `rapid_recon.enabled` (defaults to false in production).
- CLI defaults to read-only probe adapters; any write-capable probes require `--allow-writes` and explicit opt-in via environment variable.
- Telemetry retention is short-lived (48h) for recon bundles; serializer fragments do not include PII by default.

Testing and docs:
- Added a tutorial in docs/oncall/rapid-recon.md with examples for common failure classes (ingress latency, downstream timeouts, auth failures).
- Included a demo script tests/integration/test_recon_e2e.sh for local validation.

Merge outcome:
- Squash-merged to main (merge commit f3b9c2a).
- Backported the safe-mode timeout fixes to release/2026-01-legacy in a follow-up hotfix PR.

Future follow-ups (not in this PR):
- Add a lightweight UI to inspect recent recon fragments in the console.
- Add a compatibility layer so the serializer fragments can be consumed by the SLO toolkit for automated alert replays.

If you'd like to run a quick demo locally: 
1) make -C cmd/rapid-recon build
2) ./bin/rapid-recon --template=compact.yaml --timeout=10s --output=./sample-runbook.json
3) cat ./sample-runbook.json

Notes for reviewers: this bundle focused on minimal, well-scoped primitives so it can be iterated independently of the larger incident workflow.
